name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
costSource: Shorelight Best US Universities 2026 guide; HSBC most popular US states report
overview: MIT is one of the world's greatest research and teaching institutions, with an unparalleled reputation in science, engineering, mathematics, and technology that has shaped modern civilisation — from radar and the internet to digital audio and GPS. Its campus in Cambridge is dense with labs, maker spaces, and buildings designed by architectural legends including Frank Gehry and Eero Saarinen. The culture at MIT is intense and collaborative, shaped by a famous 'hacker' ethos of creative problem-solving and the occasional brilliant prank. Exchange students who are passionate about STEM will find an environment unlike any other, where the infrastructure and intellectual density push everyone to think bigger.
cityDesc: MIT sits on the northern bank of the Charles River in Cambridge, MA, directly across from Boston, giving students easy access to both the intellectual ecosystem of university-dense Cambridge and the cultural richness of one of America's most historic cities. Boston is expensive by US standards, but the MBTA connects the city well and student discounts help. The mix of history, innovation, great food, and world-class sports teams makes it a genuinely exciting place to spend a semester.

name: University of Oxford
costSource: UK Cost of Living for Students 2026 (2nd most expensive UK city); GBP/USD 1.27
overview: Oxford is one of the oldest and most prestigious universities in the world, with teaching dating back to the 12th century and a collegiate system that gives every student an intimate academic home within a larger world-class institution. The university excels across disciplines — from PPE and law to medicine, engineering, and the humanities — and its tutorial-based teaching style pushes students to think independently in a way few other universities can match. As an exchange student you'll be embedded in a college, which means a built-in social community, formal hall dinners, and access to centuries of history alongside your studies. The campus blurs seamlessly into the city, with dreaming spires, medieval libraries, and landscaped college gardens around every corner.
cityDesc: Oxford is a compact, walkable city that thrives on student life — cycling between libraries, punting on the Cherwell, and debating in centuries-old pubs is genuinely the norm here. It's more affordable than London while still offering excellent restaurants, independent shops, and strong rail links to the capital in under an hour. Exchange students almost universally fall in love with the city's atmosphere, which feels unlike anywhere else in the UK.

name: Harvard University
costSource: Harvard Housing Office 2024-25; Numbeo Cambridge MA 2025
overview: Harvard University is arguably the most famous university in the world, located in Cambridge across the Charles River from Boston, with a history stretching back to 1636 and an alumni network that includes presidents, Nobel laureates, and industry titans in virtually every field. The university's strengths are genuinely comprehensive — from law, business, and medicine to the sciences, humanities, and public policy — and the undergraduate liberal arts programme at Harvard College offers an exceptionally broad education. The campus itself is architecturally stunning, a mix of red-brick colonial buildings and modern research facilities set around Harvard Yard. Exchange students studying at Harvard find themselves surrounded by some of the most talented and driven students in the world, in an environment of remarkable intellectual energy.
cityDesc: Cambridge and Boston together form one of the most academically rich ecosystems on the planet, home to dozens of world-class universities and a culture of innovation that has produced countless breakthroughs in technology, medicine, and the social sciences. The city has superb public transit on the MBTA, excellent restaurants and nightlife across neighborhoods like Cambridge, the South End, and Fenway, and the harbour, Freedom Trail, and Charles River all add to its liveable, historic character. It's expensive by US standards, but the sheer density of opportunity — academic, professional, and cultural — is unmatched.

name: University of Cambridge

overview: Cambridge consistently ranks among the very best universities on the planet, with a collegiate system that balances world-class research with surprisingly close-knit academic communities. The university is particularly renowned for mathematics, natural sciences, engineering, and economics, and its alumni include more Nobel laureates than most countries. Exchange students are assigned to a college and quickly find that life revolves around its courts, dining hall, and sports pitches as much as the lecture theatres. The historic city centre is essentially an extension of the university, making for an immersive and unique semester experience.
cityDesc: Cambridge is a beautiful, flat city perfectly suited to cycling, with the River Cam running through the heart of it and the famous Backs — the meadows behind the colleges — offering one of the most picturesque study environments anywhere in Europe. It's smaller and quieter than London, which keeps costs down, but there's a lively bar and arts scene driven by a large student population. Most exchange students find the intimacy of the city one of its biggest strengths.

name: Imperial College London
costSource: UK Cost of Living for Students 2026 report; GBP/USD 1.27
overview: Imperial College London is a world-leading STEM university situated in South Kensington, surrounded by some of London's greatest museums including the Natural History Museum, the Science Museum, and the V&A. It is particularly outstanding in engineering, medicine, business, and the life sciences, and benefits from deep ties with London's thriving tech and biomedical industries. The campus has a compact, focused feel — most students are here to work hard — but the location in one of London's most elegant neighbourhoods means the city's energy is always on your doorstep. Exchange students who want an intensive science or engineering experience in a global capital will find it hard to beat.
cityDesc: South Kensington is one of London's most desirable neighbourhoods, rich with world-class cultural institutions, green spaces, and excellent transport links across the city via the District and Circle lines. London's cost of living is the highest in the UK, but the sheer breadth of opportunities — internships, networking events, cultural venues, and international connections — makes it compelling for ambitious exchange students. The city's size means there's always something new to explore.

name: Stanford University
costSource: University Living QS Rankings 2026 USA report (Stanford QS 3)
overview: Stanford University is one of the world's premier research universities and the academic heartbeat of Silicon Valley, with an exceptional reputation across engineering, computer science, business, medicine, law, and the humanities. Its gorgeous, sun-drenched campus — with sandstone arches, palm trees, and the iconic Hoover Tower — sprawls across over 8,000 acres in Palo Alto, creating a self-contained academic city where the lines between study, entrepreneurship, and research blur productively. Stanford's proximity to the world's leading technology companies means internship and networking opportunities are extraordinary, and the culture actively encourages students to start companies and pursue ambitious projects. Exchange students find the campus culture open, entrepreneurial, and inspiring.
cityDesc: Palo Alto and the broader San Francisco Bay Area offer exchange students one of the most exciting and diverse environments in the world — world-class tech industry networking, the cultural richness of San Francisco just 35 miles away, year-round sunshine, and easy access to the Pacific coast and mountains. The Bay Area is among the most expensive regions in the US, with housing costs particularly high, so budget planning matters. But the combination of professional opportunity, natural beauty, and cultural diversity makes it hard to beat.

name: ETH Zurich
costSource: QS Best Student Cities 2026 (Zurich top 10); CHF/USD 1.13
overview: ETH Zurich (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology) is one of the world's great science and technology universities, consistently ranked in the top five globally, with exceptional strength in mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering, computer science, and architecture — Albert Einstein studied here. The main campus in central Zurich has a compact, efficient Swiss character and is supplemented by a science campus in Hönggerberg. ETH's research output is extraordinary relative to its size, and its industry partnerships with Swiss pharmaceutical, engineering, and financial companies give students remarkable applied research opportunities. Exchange students in STEM disciplines regard ETH as one of the most intellectually rigorous and rewarding destinations in the world.
cityDesc: Zurich is consistently ranked among the world's most liveable cities — clean, efficient, safe, and surrounded by extraordinary natural beauty (the Alps are a day trip away, and the lake is stunning). It is, however, one of the most expensive cities in Europe, and exchange students need to budget very carefully for accommodation, food, and transport. That said, Zurich's cultural scene is excellent, student discounts are widely available, and the quality of life — including the ability to ski in the Alps on a weekend — is genuinely exceptional.

name: National University of Singapore

It excels across all disciplines and operates entirely in English. Singapore's strategic position makes it the gateway to Southeast Asia's rapidly growing economies.
cityDesc: Singapore is one of the world's most efficient, safe, and fascinating city-states – a seamless blend of Chinese, Malay, Indian, and Western cultures, with hawker centre food (Maxwell, Lau Pa Sat) representing some of the world's best street food at remarkably affordable prices. World's only QS top-10 university in Southeast Asia.

name: University College London

overview: University College London is one of the world's top research universities and a founding member of the prestigious Russell Group, with particular strengths in medicine, law, social sciences, architecture, and the humanities. Its main campus sits in Bloomsbury — a neighbourhood synonymous with intellectual life — and the university's ethos has always been progressive and international, making it one of the most diverse campuses in Europe. Exchange students benefit from a huge range of modules across faculties, access to London's extraordinary professional networks, and a vibrant student union. The sprawling campus blends Victorian buildings with modern research facilities across central London.
cityDesc: Bloomsbury is a wonderfully central London neighbourhood, walking distance from the British Museum, Covent Garden, and countless bookshops and cafés that make it a natural habitat for intellectually curious students. London's cost of living is high, particularly for accommodation, but student discounts, affordable food markets, and free entry to world-class museums help stretch the budget. Most exchange students find that living in London — despite the expense — is worth every penny.

Penn has a collaborative, interdisciplinary culture unusual for an elite US university, and the student body is highly engaged in both academic and community life. Exchange students benefit from access to Ivy League facilities, a global alumni network, and the considerable cultural riches of Philadelphia.

The neighbourhoods of West Philadelphia and Center City have great student bars and cafés.

name: Columbia University

overview: Columbia University is one of America's oldest and most prestigious universities and the only Ivy League institution located in New York City, giving students unparalleled access to the world's most dynamic metropolis. Its Morningside Heights campus in Upper Manhattan is architecturally magnificent — the Low Library steps are one of the iconic images of American academic life — and the university excels in law, journalism, business, medicine, international affairs, and the arts. Columbia's Core Curriculum is one of the most respected general education programmes in American higher education. Exchange students find New York City itself functions as a kind of extended campus, with internship opportunities, cultural venues, and professional networks that are simply unavailable anywhere else.
cityDesc: New York City needs no introduction — it is the world's most famous metropolis, and spending a semester here is one of the most formative experiences a student can have. Columbia's neighbourhood of Morningside Heights borders Harlem to the east and the Upper West Side to the south, offering diverse food options, parks, and easy subway access to every corner of the city. New York is expensive, and students should plan housing and living costs carefully, but there is simply no city on earth that offers more.

Exchange students experience an extraordinarily high level of academic rigour in a beautiful and supportive environment.

name: University of Toronto

Exchange students benefit from exceptional library resources, a huge range of course options, and Toronto's extraordinary cultural and professional energy.

Toronto is more expensive than Montreal, but remains affordable compared to major US cities. The natural environment of Ontario — Niagara Falls, cottage country, and the Great Lakes — is accessible from the city.

overview: EPFL (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) is a world-leading technical university on the shores of Lake Geneva, consistently ranked among the top ten universities globally for engineering and technology, with extraordinary strength in computer science, electrical engineering, materials science, life sciences, and architecture. EPFL's position in the French-speaking Swiss tech ecosystem gives students access to a remarkable density of research institutes, start-ups, and global companies. Switzerland is expensive, and Lausanne is no exception, but student cantines and subsidised housing help, and the natural environment — skiing, hiking, lake swimming — is priceless. Geneva is just 40 minutes by train for an even more international city experience.

name: Australian National University
costSource: ANU student residences 2024; Numbeo Canberra 2025
overview: Founded in 1946, ANU (QS 2025: #30) is one of the world's top 30 universities, Australia's pre-eminent research university, and the only one established by an act of the Australian parliament. It has outstanding programmes in politics, international relations, sciences, and law.
cityDesc: Canberra is Australia's purpose-built capital – clean, safe, and dominated by government institutions, think tanks, and ANU's formidable intellectual community. Sydney and Melbourne are both within 3 hours by road or 45 minutes by plane for weekend escapes.

perceptions.label: QS top-30 globally – outstanding research reputation and government access
Very safe, clean, and high quality of life in a manageable city
Canberra has limited nightlife and urban excitement
ANU students can feel isolated from Australia's major coastal cities
Strong public service and policy career connections

name: Johns Hopkins University
costSource: JHU Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Baltimore 2025
overview: Johns Hopkins University is a globally renowned research university with an exceptional reputation in medicine, public health, engineering, international studies, and the natural sciences — the Bloomberg School of Public Health is the largest and most influential public health school in the world. Its Homewood campus in north Baltimore is compact and beautifully landscaped, with a strong sense of academic community centred on the campus's Georgian revival architecture. Hopkins pioneered the modern American research university model, and that spirit of serious, original inquiry permeates every department. Exchange students find Hopkins demanding but intellectually exhilarating, with extraordinary access to research labs and faculty.
cityDesc: Baltimore is a city of distinct neighbourhoods — from the Federal Hill waterfront and the vibrant food scene of Hampden to the cultural institutions of Mount Vernon — and has undergone significant regeneration in recent years. It is considerably cheaper than Washington DC (just 40 minutes by MARC train) and New York, making it more accessible for students watching their budgets. The city's crab cakes, Chesapeake Bay culture, and underdog spirit give it a distinctive character that exchange students often find more authentic and interesting than they expected.

perceptions.label: America's #1 research university – extraordinary for pre-med and public health
Washington DC 45 minutes away – Smithsonian museums, monuments all free
Baltimore crab cakes are one of America's great culinary traditions
Baltimore has significant safety concerns – research specific areas
Hopkins' academic intensity is high – work-focused culture

name: McGill University
costSource: McGill Residences 2024-25 rates; Numbeo Montreal 2025
overview: McGill University is one of Canada's most prestigious and internationally recognised universities, with particular strengths in medicine, law, engineering, management, music, and the natural sciences — its medical school is among the best in the world, and the university has produced more Nobel laureates than any other Canadian institution. The main campus sits on the slope of Mount Royal in the heart of downtown Montreal, with a striking blend of Victorian Gothic stone buildings and modern research facilities. McGill is famously international — students come from over 150 countries — and the bilingual (English/French) character of Montreal gives the university a uniquely cosmopolitan atmosphere. Exchange students consistently rate McGill among the very best exchange experiences available anywhere.
cityDesc: Montreal is arguably the most exciting student city in North America — bilingual, culturally vibrant, and extraordinarily affordable compared to Toronto, Vancouver, or any major US city. The city's thriving music and arts scene, world-class restaurant culture (poutine and bagels are just the start), incredible summer festivals (Jazz Fest, Just for Laughs, Osheaga), and deeply French European character make it unlike anywhere else on the continent. Winters are cold and snowy, but Montrealers embrace this with joie de vivre — and skiing in the Laurentians is just over an hour away.

perceptions.label: Exceptional reputation and globally recognised degree
Montreal's nightlife and culture are unmatched in Canada
French language barrier outside campus for daily life
Harsh winters require proper preparation
Lower tuition and living costs than other top Canadian schools

name: University of Manchester
costSource: Numbeo Manchester 2025; UoM Accommodation Services rates
overview: The University of Manchester is a powerhouse research institution — home to 25 Nobel laureates including Ernest Rutherford and Andre Geim — with particular strengths in science, engineering, business, humanities, and social sciences. Its large campus in the Oxford Road Corridor sits just south of the city centre and has a lively, energetic feel driven by one of the largest student populations in the UK. The university invented the computer and split the atom here, and that spirit of innovation continues in its world-class laboratories and business partnerships. Exchange students quickly find Manchester's relaxed, welcoming culture makes it one of the easiest places to settle into student life.
cityDesc: Manchester is one of the UK's most vibrant and affordable cities — famously proud of its music heritage (The Smiths, Oasis, The Haçienda), its football culture, and its packed social calendar. Accommodation and living costs are among the most reasonable of any major UK university city, which means exchange students can enjoy excellent restaurants, bars, and live venues without breaking the bank. The Northern Quarter and Ancoats are particularly beloved by students for their independent coffee shops, street food, and nightlife.

perceptions.label: QS top-35 university with extraordinary Nobel Prize heritage
UK's best music scene – from Joy Division to Oasis, Manchester defines British rock
More affordable than London – similar quality of life at lower cost
Grey, rainy climate – Manchester has a reputation for being wet
City centre can be rough in some areas late at night

name: University of Hong Kong
costSource: HKU Housing Division 2024; Numbeo Hong Kong 2025; HKD/USD ~0.128
overview: Founded in 1911, the University of Hong Kong (QS 2025: #36) is Asia's most internationally oriented top-40 university. It operates entirely in English and has an outstanding reputation across law, medicine, business, and the social sciences.
cityDesc: Hong Kong is one of the world's great cities – a vertical forest of skyscrapers above Victoria Harbour, some of the world's finest dim sum, hiking trails through country parks accessible by MTR, and a unique East-meets-West cultural blend. Despite political changes since 2020, it remains a major global financial centre.

perceptions.label: QS top-40 global university with full English-medium instruction
Hong Kong's dim sum and Cantonese food culture is extraordinary
World's most efficient public transport (Octopus Card MTR)
Hong Kong is one of the world's most expensive cities
Political situation has changed significantly since 2020 – worth researching current context

name: Monash University
costSource: Monash student residences 2024; Numbeo Melbourne 2025
overview: Founded in 1958, Monash University (QS 2025: #37) is Australia's second-ranked university and one of its most internationally connected, with campuses in Melbourne, Malaysia, and South Africa. It has strong programmes in pharmacy, engineering, business, and law.
cityDesc: Monash's main Clayton campus is in Melbourne's southeastern suburbs, connected to the CBD by train. Students access all of Melbourne's outstanding café, arts, and sporting culture while benefiting from a large campus with significant research facilities.

perceptions.label: One of Australia's most international campuses – truly global student community
Access to all of Melbourne's outstanding lifestyle offerings
Clayton campus is suburban – requires transport to reach central Melbourne
Australian costs are high
Strong research output across medicine, pharmacy, and engineering

name: University of British Columbia
costSource: UBC Student Housing rates 2024-25; Numbeo Vancouver 2025
overview: The University of British Columbia in Vancouver is one of Canada's top two universities and a major global research institution, with world-class programmes in medicine, science, engineering, forestry, arts, law, and business — and a campus setting that is among the most spectacular of any university in the world, perched on a forested point of land between the Pacific Ocean and the Coast Mountains. UBC's research output and innovation credentials place it firmly in the global top 40, and its proximity to Vancouver's technology sector (home to major game studios, tech firms, and a growing biotech industry) provides extraordinary professional development opportunities. Exchange students are immediately struck by the combination of academic seriousness and natural beauty.
cityDesc: Vancouver is one of the world's most beautiful cities — set between mountains and the Pacific, with a mild, if rainy, climate and an extraordinary outdoor lifestyle that includes skiing, hiking, kayaking, and cycling year-round. The food scene is outstanding, driven by an incredibly diverse population and the quality of Pacific seafood and Asian cuisine. It is, however, one of the most expensive cities in Canada, with housing costs that are among the highest in North America — budget planning is important. The campus itself has beaches, trails, and stunning mountain views that make the day-to-day student experience genuinely exceptional.

perceptions.label: Stunning campus setting between mountains and ocean
World-class research environment and co-op programmes
Very high cost of living, especially rent
Campus can feel isolated from downtown Vancouver
Excellent outdoor recreation year-round

name: New York University
costSource: University Living top 10 US universities for international students report (NYU 27% international)
overview: NYU ranks 39th globally (QS 2025), with campuses in Manhattan and Brooklyn, and approximately 27% of its student body international.
cityDesc: New York City offers an unmatched concentration of culture, nightlife, and food from every corner of the world, alongside the highest concentration of internship and career opportunities in the US. It's also one of the most expensive cities on Earth to live in.

perceptions.label: Unmatched culture, food, and nightlife density
Best internship/career access in the US
Incredibly walkable, strong public transit
Among the most expensive cities in the world
Cold winters

name: Fudan University
costSource: Fudan International Students Center 2024; Numbeo Shanghai 2025; CNY/USD ~0.138
overview: Founded in 1905, Fudan University (QS 2025: #39) is one of China's most prestigious universities and frequently ranks as its #2 or #3 institution. It has particular strengths in the humanities, social sciences, law, and management, and is the most internationally recognized name in Chinese humanities education.
cityDesc: Fudan's campus is in Yangpu district, steps from the French Concession's tree-lined streets, Art Deco architecture, and some of Shanghai's best restaurants and bars. Shanghai is China's most international city – the Bund, Pudong's skyline, Old Town's gardens, and the Longtang alleyways create an extraordinary urban texture.

perceptions.label: China's most prestigious humanities and social science university
French Concession location gives access to Shanghai's best dining and nightlife
Extraordinary affordability – one of the world's cheapest major cities for students

Mandarin strongly recommended – though Shanghai has more English than Beijing

name: King's College London
costSource: Numbeo London 2025; KCL Student Accommodation Services
overview: King's College London is one of the oldest and most distinguished universities in the UK, with particular strengths in medicine, law, nursing, dentistry, humanities, and the social sciences. Its campuses are spread along the South Bank and the Strand in central London, offering some of the most spectacular river views in the city and easy access to the cultural heart of the capital. King's has deep historical roots — it was founded by royal charter in 1829 — and carries a sense of tradition alongside genuinely cutting-edge research. Exchange students are spread across multiple faculties and tend to appreciate the urban, cosmopolitan campus life.
cityDesc: King's campuses along the Thames put students right at the centre of London's cultural life — the Tate Modern, Shakespeare's Globe, the National Theatre, and Borough Market are all within a short walk. London is the most expensive city in the UK, so accommodation costs should be planned for carefully, but the diversity of experiences on offer makes it one of the most rewarding places in the world to spend a semester. The South Bank is particularly lively with free events and markets year-round.

perceptions.label: QS top-40 university in the world's most globally connected city
Campus is literally in the heart of London – unbeatable location
London's career opportunities in finance, law, and media are without equal
London is one of the world's most expensive cities for students
Finding affordable accommodation in London is genuinely difficult

name: Seoul National University
costSource: SNU International Office housing data 2024; Numbeo Seoul 2025; KRW/USD ~0.00075
overview: Founded in 1946, Seoul National University (QS 2025: #41) is South Korea's most prestigious university and a leading East Asian institution. It excels in engineering, natural sciences, business, and law, and produces a disproportionate share of South Korea's political and business leaders.
cityDesc: Seoul is one of Asia's most exciting cities – a hyper-modern, hyper-efficient megalopolis with the world's best fried chicken, Korean BBQ on every corner, Gangnam's luxury culture, Hongdae's art-student nightlife, and one of the world's best public transport systems (T-money card).

perceptions.label: Korea's #1 university with extraordinary career prestige in East Asia
Korean food is genuinely one of the world's great culinary traditions
Seoul is one of Asia's safest and most efficient major cities

Winters are cold (below -10°C) and summers humid

name: University of Queensland
costSource: UQ Housing 2024; Numbeo Brisbane 2025
overview: Founded in 1909, the University of Queensland (QS 2025: #40) is one of Australia's Group of Eight elite universities and consistently ranks in the global top 50. Its St Lucia campus on a bend of the Brisbane River is one of Australia's most beautiful. It has outstanding programmes in medicine, agriculture, mining engineering, and biological sciences.
cityDesc: Brisbane is Queensland's subtropical capital – warm, outdoor-focused, and increasingly vibrant after hosting the 2032 Summer Olympics planning cycle. The Great Barrier Reef is 2 hours by plane. The Gold Coast's beaches (Surfers Paradise) are 1 hour south. Noosa and the Sunshine Coast are 1.5 hours north.

name: Kyoto University
costSource: Kyoto University ILAS programme housing data 2024; Numbeo Kyoto 2025
overview: Founded in 1897, Kyoto University (QS 2025: #46) is Japan's second-ranked university and has produced more Nobel Prize winners than any other Asian university. It has particular strengths in natural sciences, mathematics, and engineering.
cityDesc: Kyoto is Japan's most culturally extraordinary city – 1,000 temples, Geisha districts (Gion), the most beautiful bamboo grove in the world (Arashiyama), and 17 UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Nara (deer park) is 45 minutes away; Osaka 15 minutes.

perceptions.label: Most Nobel Prize winners of any Asian university
Kyoto is Japan's most culturally and historically rich city

Gion Matsuri festival (July 17) — Japan's most spectacular festival

name: Chinese University of Hong Kong
costSource: CUHK housing office 2024; Numbeo Hong Kong 2025
overview: Founded in 1963, the Chinese University of Hong Kong (QS 2025: #47) is a leading bilingual (English and Chinese) research university in Hong Kong. It has strong programmes in business, medicine, and the humanities, and its mountain campus with harbour views is exceptional.
cityDesc: CUHK's campus rises up the hills of the New Territories with spectacular views over Tolo Harbour. The university is more connected to Chinese culture than HKU, offering exchange students deeper access to Hong Kong's Cantonese cultural identity alongside an English-medium academic environment.

name: Zhejiang University
costSource: ZJU International College housing 2024; Numbeo Hangzhou 2025; CNY/USD ~0.138
overview: Founded in 1897, Zhejiang University (QS 2025: #47) is one of China's five most prestigious universities and is ranked in the global top 50. It has outstanding programmes across engineering, medicine, agronomy, and the sciences, and benefits from being in Hangzhou – one of China's most beautiful cities.
cityDesc: Hangzhou is arguably China's most beautiful city – West Lake (UNESCO World Heritage) is genuinely extraordinary, with willow-fringed causeways, ancient pagodas, and tea plantations on the surrounding hills. It is also China's e-commerce capital (home of Alibaba). Shanghai is 1 hour by high-speed rail.

name: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
costSource: HKUST housing 2024; Numbeo Hong Kong 2025
overview: Founded in 1991, HKUST (QS 2025: #47) is one of the world's top 50 universities – remarkable for such a young institution. Its cliff-top campus overlooking Clearwater Bay has the most beautiful setting of any major university in Asia, and it excels in engineering, science, and business.
cityDesc: HKUST's Clearwater Bay campus hangs above the South China Sea on Hong Kong's eastern coast, with direct sea-view from virtually every classroom. The campus has its own beach and sea sports facilities, while the MTR connects to Hong Kong's full urban offering in 40 minutes.

Most beautiful campus setting in Asia – cliff-top above the South China Sea

name: Delft University of Technology
costSource: University data + Numbeo
overview: Delft University of Technology is the largest and most research-intensive technical university in the Netherlands, with a global reputation in aerospace engineering, civil engineering, industrial design, architecture, applied mathematics, and computer science. The campus in Delft has been transformed in recent decades into a striking modern complex centred on the iconic Library building with its grass-covered roof, surrounded by innovation centres and start-up incubators. TU Delft's collaborations with the Dutch water management, energy, and technology industries are world-leading. Exchange students in engineering, design, or technology disciplines find TU Delft one of the most stimulating and industry-connected universities in Europe.
cityDesc: Delft is a charming, compact Dutch city famous for its blue-and-white Delftware pottery and one of the best-preserved historic city centres in the Netherlands — canals, gabled houses, and the Old Church all within cycling distance of campus. It is less expensive than Amsterdam and Rotterdam and has a strong student café culture. Rotterdam (10 minutes by train) is one of Europe's great modern architecture cities, and the Hague and Amsterdam are both easily accessible, giving Delft students a remarkably rich surrounding region to explore.

perceptions.label: Active exchange community
Strong academics
Good transport links
Adjustment period
Competitive environment

name: Shanghai Jiao Tong University
costSource: SJTU International Students Office housing 2024; Numbeo Shanghai 2025
overview: Founded in 1896, Shanghai Jiao Tong University (QS 2025: #47) is China's leading engineering and technology university, renowned for the Shanghai Ranking's Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) which SJTU created. It has particular strengths in engineering, medicine, and management.
cityDesc: Shanghai is China's most international and cosmopolitan city – a global financial centre where East meets West most dramatically. The Bund's Art Deco facades across from Pudong's futuristic skyline, French Concession tree-lined streets, and the world's fastest maglev train make Shanghai uniquely exciting.

perceptions.label: China's top engineering university in its most international city
Shanghai is China's most liveable city for international students

name: London School of Economics and Political Science
costSource: Numbeo London 2025; LSE student accommodation
overview: The London School of Economics and Political Science is one of the world's leading social science universities, with an unrivalled reputation in economics, politics, law, sociology, and international relations. Its central London location on the edge of the City and just minutes from Westminster means students are surrounded by the institutions they study — law courts, parliament, think tanks, and global financial firms are all nearby. The school has a famously international student body, and the intellectual atmosphere is intense and stimulating. Exchange students come from over 100 countries, making LSE one of the most cosmopolitan campuses anywhere.
cityDesc: LSE sits between Holborn and the Strand in central London, with the City of London and the West End both within easy walking distance — an ideal position for students interested in finance, policy, law, or media. London is expensive, but the concentration of internship and networking opportunities is unmatched anywhere in Europe. The city's vast cultural scene, multicultural food options, and excellent public transport make it endlessly liveable.

perceptions.label: World-class career networking – LSE in central London is unbeatable for internships
Very high cost of living – one of the most expensive student cities globally
Intense academic culture with a politically engaged, globally diverse student body

name: Northwestern University
costSource: Northwestern Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Evanston 2025
overview: Northwestern University is a leading private research university in Evanston, Illinois — just north of Chicago along Lake Michigan — with exceptional strengths in journalism, theatre, law, medicine, economics, engineering, and the social sciences. Its campus, spread along the lakefront with beautiful views of Lake Michigan, has a distinctive physical character and a vibrant community feel driven by one of the strongest Greek life and performing arts scenes among elite US universities. Northwestern benefits greatly from its proximity to Chicago, which functions as an extended campus for internship opportunities, cultural experiences, and professional networking. Exchange students find the balance between high academic expectations and a rich campus social life compelling.
cityDesc: Evanston is a charming, walkable university town with excellent restaurants, independent shops, and a lively cafe culture, and it sits on the METRA and 'L' Purple Line — meaning downtown Chicago is just 45 minutes away by transit. Chicago offers world-class food, architecture, music, and arts at costs significantly below New York or San Francisco. The Lake Michigan lakefront is beautiful and accessible year-round, with beaches and parks that students flock to in warmer months.

perceptions.label: Stunning Lake Michigan campus – one of America's most beautiful waterfront settings
Chicago 30 minutes away by train – exceptional city access
Outstanding journalism (Medill) and business (Kellogg) schools
Evanston itself is quiet – most social life requires heading to Chicago

name: KAIST
costSource: KAIST scholarship/housing office 2024; Numbeo Daejeon 2025
overview: Founded in 1971, KAIST (QS 2025: #63) is South Korea's leading science and technology university and one of Asia's top STEM institutions. Most programmes are taught in English, and scholarships are widely available for international students.
cityDesc: Daejeon is South Korea's science city – compact, affordable, and home to most of South Korea's major research institutions. While quieter than Seoul (45 minutes by KTX bullet train), KAIST's campus provides intensive research culture with many English-speaking students and faculty.

name: University of Bristol
costSource: Numbeo Bristol 2025; University of Bristol Student Accommodation
overview: The University of Bristol is a leading research university and Russell Group member with a beautiful hillside campus overlooking the city, known for its strong culture of student wellbeing and a social scene that blends academic ambition with a love of the outdoors. Bristol is particularly strong in engineering, medicine, law, economics, and the creative arts, and benefits from close industry ties in aerospace, fintech, and the life sciences. The university has a friendly, approachable atmosphere — Clifton, the neighbourhood surrounding the main campus, is one of the most desirable student areas in the UK. Exchange students consistently rate Bristol among their top destinations in England.
cityDesc: Bristol is a creative, independent-spirited city with a thriving arts and music scene, excellent food culture centred around St Nicholas Market, and a strong tradition of street art (Banksy grew up here). Costs are lower than London but higher than cities further north, and the city rewards exploration — from the harbourside and Clifton Suspension Bridge to the rolling hills of the surrounding countryside. The city's compact size and friendly atmosphere make it very easy to feel at home.

More affordable than London, better located than Manchester

cityDesc: Champaign-Urbana is a classic Midwestern college town – flat, affordable, and entirely shaped by the university. While it lacks big-city amenities, the engineering and CS culture is intensely strong.

name: University of Amsterdam
costSource: University of Amsterdam official living expenses page (uva.nl); HousingAnywhere rent data; EUR/USD 1.087
overview: The University of Amsterdam is one of the largest and most internationally respected universities in the Netherlands, with particular strengths in economics, law, social sciences, humanities, and natural sciences — and one of the highest proportions of English-language programmes of any continental European university. Its buildings are distributed throughout the historic canal-ring centre of Amsterdam, meaning students study in 17th-century merchant houses and cutting-edge modern buildings within the same campus tour. UvA is part of a rich academic ecosystem that includes the Amsterdam Medical Centre and close collaboration with industry. Exchange students find Amsterdam one of the most cosmopolitan and enjoyable study destinations in Europe.
cityDesc: Amsterdam needs little introduction — its canal network, world-class museums (the Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum, and Anne Frank House), cycling culture, and extraordinarily diverse and tolerant social culture make it one of Europe's most beloved cities. It is not cheap — accommodation in particular is very expensive and requires advance planning — but student housing systems and the strong supply of English-speaking services make it manageable. The Netherlands' superb rail network means Rotterdam, the Hague, Utrecht, and Leiden are all under an hour away.

It has particular strengths in design (School of Design is world-class), hospitality, and applied sciences, and its Hung Hom campus is a short walk from major MTR connections.

name: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich
costSource: Studying-in-Germany.org 2025-26 report (budget EUR1,200-1,500/mo); EUR/USD 1.087
overview: Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich is Germany's largest and most prestigious university, founded in 1472, with exceptional strength across the natural sciences, medicine, law, economics, social sciences, and the humanities — it consistently ranks among the top universities in continental Europe. The main campus sits in the Maxvorstadt district, Munich's museum and gallery quarter, with grand Neoclassical buildings and a campus culture that blends serious academic rigour with the Bavarian love of good food and community. LMU has produced a remarkable number of Nobel laureates and remains a major force in European research. Exchange students from around the world are drawn by the combination of academic excellence, city culture, and Germany's generally affordable student life.
cityDesc: Munich is one of Europe's most beautiful and liveable cities — the Bavarian capital is wealthy, clean, and spectacularly well-organised, with outstanding public transport, a world-famous beer garden and Oktoberfest culture, stunning Baroque architecture, and the Alps less than an hour to the south. The cost of living is high by German standards — Munich rivals Amsterdam or Zurich for housing costs — but the quality of life is exceptional and the city's student population keeps the food and nightlife scene vibrant. The English Garden, one of the world's largest urban parks, is effectively LMU's backyard.

name: École Polytechnique
costSource: X housing 2024; Numbeo Paris 2025
overview: École Polytechnique is France's most prestigious grande école for mathematics, physics, engineering, and the sciences, producing many of the country's top scientists, engineers, and public leaders. Founded in 1794 by revolutionary France and with a military tradition that persists in its culture, Polytechnique combines an exceptionally rigorous scientific curriculum with a unique residential college model on its campus in Palaiseau, south of Paris. The student body is small and highly selective — X (as it is known) graduates are a byword for intellectual excellence in French industry and government. Exchange students accepted at Polytechnique join one of the most exclusive and intellectually intense academic environments in Europe.
cityDesc: Polytechnique's campus in Palaiseau is about 25 kilometres south of central Paris, in the heart of the Paris-Saclay technology cluster — one of the most significant concentrations of research institutions and technology companies in Europe. The campus is self-contained and residential, which creates a close-knit community, and the RER B train connects it to central Paris in about 45 minutes. Paris offers everything the world's greatest city has to offer on weekends, while daily life on the campus plateau has a focused, purposeful character.

name: Duke University
costSource: Duke University housing.duke.edu 2024-25; Numbeo Durham 2025
overview: Duke University is one of America's leading private research universities, with outstanding programmes in medicine, law, public policy, engineering, environmental science, and business, and a global reputation for both academic excellence and an extraordinary undergraduate experience. Its stunning Gothic-influenced West Campus in Durham, North Carolina, was built in the early 20th century and gives Duke a distinctive, almost European grandeur. Duke is also famous for the Cameron Indoor Stadium and its basketball culture — the Blue Devils are one of college basketball's most iconic teams, and game nights generate an electric campus atmosphere. Exchange students find Duke's campus beautiful, its faculty remarkably accessible, and the Research Triangle an exciting intellectual environment.

The broader Triangle area has seen rapid growth in recent years and offers excellent restaurants, a thriving live music scene, and outdoor activities in the nearby piedmont and mountains. Living costs are well below the US coastal cities, making Duke excellent value despite its elite status.

name: Sorbonne University

overview: Sorbonne University (Sorbonne Université) is one of the world's most iconic academic institutions — the name alone carries centuries of intellectual history — formed in 2018 through the merger of Paris-Sorbonne (Paris IV) and Pierre and Marie Curie University (Paris VI), creating one of France's largest and most comprehensive research universities. It is particularly strong in literature, history, philosophy, languages, medicine, and the natural sciences. Exchange students at Sorbonne are immersed in the heart of French intellectual and cultural life.

Paris is expensive, particularly for accommodation, but student subsidies through the CROUS system and the RER/Metro network make it more manageable than it appears. The city's cultural offering — 130 museums, outstanding food, fashion, and a nightlife scene that runs from wine bars to world-class clubs — makes Paris one of the most coveted exchange destinations on earth.

name: University of Warwick

Warwick is famous for its entrepreneurial spirit and has spun out more start-ups than almost any other UK university. Exchange students appreciate the tight-knit campus community and the very active Students' Union, which hosts one of the UK's largest student entertainment programmes.
cityDesc: While Warwick's campus is technically in Coventry, students have easy access to both Coventry (a rapidly regenerating city with good transport links) and Leamington Spa, a Regency-era spa town just a short bus ride away with charming cafés and restaurants. Living costs are noticeably lower than London or Bristol, making Warwick excellent value for exchange students.

name: Heidelberg University

Heidelberg's research in molecular biology, physics, and the humanities is internationally recognised, and its student culture retains a strong sense of tradition alongside cutting-edge academic work. Exchange students find Heidelberg an extraordinarily atmospheric and intellectually stimulating place to study.
cityDesc: Heidelberg is often called one of the most beautiful cities in Germany — its castle ruins, Baroque old town, and the Neckar River flowing beneath the Philosopher's Walk create a setting that has inspired poets and painters for centuries. Frankfurt, one of Europe's major financial and transport hubs, is just one hour away by train, making Heidelberg an excellent base. Costs are moderate by German standards.

The university's global outlook is reflected in a diverse, multicultural campus.

overview: Founded in 1876, Hokkaido University (QS 2025: #170) is Japan's northernmost research university, with world-leading programmes in agriculture, veterinary science, fisheries, and environmental science. Its Sapporo campus – a former American-style land-grant college – is Japan's most spacious and beautiful.
cityDesc: Sapporo is Hokkaido's capital – Japan's largest northern island, defined by extraordinary winters (the Snow Festival in February draws 2 million visitors), world-class skiing (Niseko resort is 90 minutes away, rated Asia's best powder snow), and unrivalled seafood (crab, sea urchin, salmon). Summers are cool and green – perfect hiking in Daisetsuzan National Park.

perceptions.label: Niseko ski resort 90 minutes away – Asia's most acclaimed powder snow skiing
Sapporo Snow Festival (February) is one of Asia's most spectacular events
Hokkaido seafood – crab, uni, salmon – is Japan's finest
Japanese language required for most courses
Hokkaido winters are very cold and snowy – commitment required

Cherry blossoms on campus (early May in Hokkaido)
Sapporo Snow Festival — largest winter event in Japan

name: Curtin University
costSource: Curtin Housing 2024; Numbeo Perth 2025
overview: Founded in 1966, Curtin University (QS 2025: #188) is Western Australia's largest university and globally strong in mining engineering, petroleum engineering, and business. Its Bentley campus in Perth is 10 minutes from the city and within easy reach of Perth's extraordinary beaches.
cityDesc: Perth is the world's most remote major city – 4 hours from Adelaide, 5 from Sydney. But this isolation creates a unique culture: world-class Indian Ocean beaches (Cottesloe, Scarborough), world-class wineries in the Swan Valley and Margaret River (3 hours south), and remarkable wildflower season (August-October) in the surrounding bushland.

Indian Ocean beaches within 20 minutes – among Australia's finest
Margaret River wine region 3 hours south – world-class

name: Autonomous University of Barcelona
costSource: Numbeo Barcelona 2025; UAB International Welcome Point housing guide
overview: Founded in 1968, the Autonomous University of Barcelona (QS 2025: #201) is one of Spain's leading research universities, ranked among the top 10 in the Iberian Peninsula. It excels in biosciences, economics, law, and the social sciences, and hosts one of Europe's largest Erasmus communities.
cityDesc: UAB's self-contained campus sits 20km north of Barcelona, connected by suburban train to the city. Students can access Barcelona's beaches, Gothic Quarter, and legendary nightlife within 30 minutes, combining campus tranquility with big-city excitement.

perceptions.label: Best of both worlds – campus calm and Barcelona's urban energy
One of Europe's most active Erasmus communities
Campus location means commuting to Barcelona for nightlife
Spanish and Catalan both essential – English courses available but limited
Excellent weather and Mediterranean quality of life

name: McMaster University
costSource: McMaster Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Hamilton ON 2025; CAD/USD ~0.74
overview: Founded in 1887, McMaster University (QS 2025: #189) is one of Canada's leading research universities, with a global reputation for its problem-based medical education model (adopted worldwide) and its DeGroote Business School. It consistently ranks in the global top 200.
cityDesc: Hamilton is a post-industrial Ontario city undergoing a remarkable arts-led revival – the James Street North arts corridor, the Royal Botanical Gardens, and the Niagara Escarpment hiking (Bruce Trail) are all within easy reach. Niagara Falls is 45 minutes. Toronto is 60 minutes by GO Train.

perceptions.label: Problem-based medical learning model – world-leading innovation in health sciences
Niagara Falls 45 minutes, Toronto 60 minutes by GO Train
Hamilton's arts revival is genuine and affordable
Hamilton is still gentrifying – some rough areas outside the arts corridors
Ontario winters are cold and snowy

name: Newcastle University
costSource: Newcastle University accommodation 2024; Numbeo Newcastle 2025
overview: Newcastle University is a leading Russell Group university with particular strengths in medicine, engineering, architecture, marine science, and the arts, set within a beautiful Victorian campus in the heart of Newcastle city centre. It has one of the most active and celebrated student communities in the UK, reflecting the city's famously warm and welcoming culture — the 'Geordie' hospitality is not a myth. Research at Newcastle is globally significant, particularly in ageing, medicine, and sustainability, and the university's urban location gives students extraordinary access to professional networks and cultural life. Exchange students consistently rate Newcastle among the most enjoyable exchange destinations in England.
cityDesc: Newcastle is famous for two things among students: its legendary nightlife (the Bigg Market and Quayside clubs are an institution) and the extraordinary friendliness of the locals. The cost of living is among the lowest of any major UK city, meaning exchange students can eat, drink, and travel without the financial stress common in London or Edinburgh. The city's waterfront, independent restaurant scene, and easy access to Northumberland's stunning coastline and countryside round out what is a genuinely exceptional exchange destination.

perceptions.label: Britain's friendliest city with extraordinary student nightlife scene
Hadrian's Wall and Northumberland's wild coast within 1 hour
More affordable than London with a strong Russell Group university
Newcastle weather is cold and wet
Geordie accent takes adjustment even for native English speakers

name: University of Newcastle
costSource: University data + Numbeo
overview: The University of Newcastle is a leading Australian research university ranked in the global top 200. Located between Sydney and the world-famous Hunter Valley wine region, Newcastle is a relaxed coastal city with outstanding surf beaches, a thriving arts and cafe scene, and day trips to the Blue Mountains. Exchange students get serious academics with a genuinely beautiful lifestyle.
cityDesc: Newcastle is a large city known for its beachy atmosphere.

name: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia
costSource: UTM housing 2024; Numbeo Johor Bahru 2025; MYR/USD ~0.226
overview: Founded in 1904, Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (QS 2025: #195) is Malaysia's leading technology university and Southeast Asia's top engineering school, with exceptional programmes in civil, electrical, and mechanical engineering. Its Johor Bahru campus is 1 hour by bus from Singapore.
cityDesc: Johor Bahru sits on the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula – Singapore is literally across the causeway (1km), accessible by bus or train in under an hour. This gives UTM students access to both Malaysia's lower costs and Singapore's world-class infrastructure. The Johor coast, Desaru Beach, and Tioman Island are accessible for weekends.

perceptions.label: Singapore literally across the causeway – best of both Malaysia and Singapore
QS top-200 at extremely affordable Malaysian costs
Gateway to Tioman Island and Malaysia's extraordinary marine parks
Johor Bahru city itself lacks character compared to KL or Singapore

name: Waseda University

overview: Waseda is one of Japan's most prestigious private universities (QS rank 196, 2025), located in Shinjuku, Tokyo, one of QS's top 2 Best Student Cities globally.
cityDesc: Tokyo's day-to-day costs are lower than most Western students expect. Domestic travel via Shinkansen adds up fast. The city is remarkably safe by any global standard.

Extraordinary food at every price point
One of the safest cities on Earth

name: University of York
costSource: York Housing 2024-25; Numbeo York 2025
overview: The University of York is a highly rated research university set on a striking, architect-designed campus around an artificial lake south of the historic city centre. It is particularly strong in biology, chemistry, politics, history, English, archaeology, and social policy, and benefits from a collegiate system that gives every student an immediate social community on a campus known for its inclusive, friendly culture. York has produced world-leading research in healthcare, environment, and social sciences. Exchange students consistently rate York as one of the most enjoyable and well-supported exchange destinations in the UK.
cityDesc: York is one of England's most beautiful and historic cities — its medieval walls are intact, the Shambles is one of the best-preserved medieval streets in Europe, and York Minster is a Gothic masterpiece. The city is compact and very walkable, with a great selection of pubs, restaurants, and independent shops, and living costs are comfortably below the national average. It's well-connected by rail to Leeds (20 minutes), Manchester, and London (under 2 hours), making it easy to explore the wider country.

perceptions.label: York is arguably England's most beautiful historic city
Medieval walls, Viking heritage, and the Shambles – genuinely extraordinary history
Yorkshire Moors and Dales hiking within 30 minutes
York is quiet for a university city – nightlife is limited

name: Tecnológico de Monterrey (ITESM)
costSource: Tec de Monterrey Campus Housing Office 2024; Numbeo Monterrey 2025
overview: Founded in 1943, Tecnológico de Monterrey (QS 2025: #184) is the leading private university in Mexico and one of Latin America's top institutions. The flagship Monterrey campus excels in engineering, business, and technology.
cityDesc: Monterrey is Mexico's most industrialised city, a major business hub near the US border with a growing craft beer and culinary scene, surrounded by dramatic Sierra Madre mountains.

perceptions.label: Leading private university in Latin America with global ties
Strong industry connections in Mexico's manufacturing and business sector
Summer heat in Monterrey is extreme
Spanish is dominant – English programmes exist but social life is Spanish

name: Cardiff University
costSource: Cardiff University accommodation 2024; Numbeo Cardiff 2025
overview: Cardiff University is Wales's leading research university and a Russell Group member, with particular strengths in medicine, journalism, engineering, law, and the social sciences. Its main campus borders Cathays Park — Cardiff's civic heart, home to the Welsh Assembly and Edwardian-era museums — and has a grand, confident architectural feel. The university is notably strong in Welsh language provision and Celtic studies, alongside a fully modern research programme. Exchange students find Cardiff easy to settle into: the city is compact, the people are famously friendly, and student life has a vibrant, community feel centred around Cathays and Roath.
cityDesc: Cardiff is one of Europe's youngest capital cities and has transformed enormously in recent decades — the waterfront Cardiff Bay area, the Victorian arcades, and a buzzing food and nightlife scene all make it an exciting place to live. It is significantly cheaper than London, Bristol, or Edinburgh, offering excellent value for exchange students on a budget. Wales's stunning national parks — including the Brecon Beacons and the Pembrokeshire coast — are within easy reach for weekend adventures.

perceptions.label: Youngest capital in Europe with a castle in the city centre
Brecon Beacons and Gower Peninsula beaches both within 45 minutes
More affordable than most major UK university cities
Cardiff's Welsh-medium culture is distinct but English is universal
UK costs still significant compared to continental Europe

events: Six Nations Rugby (February/March) — Cardiff becomes rugby's global capital

name: Keio University
costSource: Keio IES housing data 2024; Numbeo Tokyo 2025; JPY/USD ~0.0067
overview: Founded in 1858 by Yukichi Fukuzawa (whose face is on the ¥10,000 note), Keio University (QS 2025: #189) is Japan's oldest and most prestigious private university. Its alumni dominate Japanese business, media, and government. The Mita campus in Minato-ku is surrounded by Tokyo's business heart.
cityDesc: Keio students access all of Tokyo's extraordinary offerings – the world's most Michelin stars, the safest major city on Earth, cherry blossoms in spring, Shibuya crossing's orchestrated chaos, and day trips to Nikko, Kamakura, and Mount Fuji. Japan's unique blend of ultra-modernity and deep tradition is endlessly fascinating.

Mita campus is in the heart of Tokyo's business and diplomatic district
Japan offers the world's most extraordinary combination of safety and culture

name: University of Ottawa
costSource: uOttawa Housing housing.uottawa.ca 2024-25; Numbeo Ottawa 2025; CAD/USD ~0.73
overview: Founded in 1848, the University of Ottawa (QS 2025: #601 band) is the world's largest bilingual (English-French) university and a leading Canadian research institution. Its location 500 metres from Parliament Hill and the Supreme Court of Canada provides unmatched access to Canada's political and legal institutions.
cityDesc: uOttawa sits at the heart of Canada's capital, steps from Parliament Hill. As a bilingual institution, it's the best place in Canada to develop or practice French while studying at an English-medium university. The campus overlooks the Rideau River and is walking distance from the Byward Market.

perceptions.label: World's largest bilingual (English-French) university – ideal for French immersion
500 metres from Canada's Parliament – political access is extraordinary

name: TU Wien
costSource: TU Wien housing 2024; Numbeo Vienna 2025
overview: TU Wien (Vienna University of Technology) is Austria's leading technical university, with outstanding programmes in architecture, engineering, computer science, mathematics, physics, and chemistry — and a long history of research excellence reflected in its distinguished alumni. The main campus occupies elegant 19th-century buildings in Vienna's 4th district, just south of the Ringstrasse, in a position that places students right in the heart of one of Europe's greatest cities. TU Wien has deep connections to Austrian and Central European industry and benefits from the broader intellectual ecosystem of a city with multiple world-class universities. Exchange students in engineering, technology, or architecture find Vienna a truly exceptional setting.
cityDesc: Vienna's 4th and 1st districts — where TU Wien's buildings are concentrated — are some of the most beautiful and historically layered urban environments in the world, within walking distance of the Naschmarkt (Vienna's famous outdoor market), the Ringstrasse museums, and the historic first district. Vienna is a city of extraordinary quality of life, remarkable affordability relative to other Western European capitals, and a cultural depth that rewards months of exploration. The Austrian Alps and Hungarian border are both within easy day trip distance.

perceptions.label: Vienna is consistently voted world's most liveable city
Habsburg imperial culture – palaces, opera, coffee houses – is extraordinary
Central Europe transit hub – Budapest, Prague, Bratislava all within 4 hours

name: University of Hamburg
costSource: Numbeo Hamburg 2025; Studierendenwerk Hamburg housing data
overview: The University of Hamburg is northern Germany's largest university, with strong programmes in law, economics, natural sciences, medicine, and the humanities — and a research environment shaped by Hamburg's role as Germany's gateway to the world. The main campus in the Rotherbaum neighbourhood is surrounded by the beautiful Außenalster lake and has a distinguished, classical character. Hamburg's ties to international trade, media, and cultural industries give the university's social and legal programmes particular real-world relevance. Exchange students find Hamburg a sophisticated, outward-looking city that makes for a very enjoyable semester.
cityDesc: Hamburg is Germany's second-largest city and one of its most international — a major port city with a cosmopolitan food scene, legendary nightlife (the Reeperbahn and Schanzenviertel districts), a world-famous concert hall (the Elbphilharmonie), and the Speicherstadt warehouse district that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Living costs are moderate by Western European standards, though higher than Berlin, and the city's excellent public transport network makes it very navigable. Hamburg's harbour setting and Scandinavian-inflected culture give it a distinct, open-sea atmosphere.

perceptions.label: One of Germany's most vibrant nightlife cities
Beautiful harbour and lake-filled cityscape
Germany's wealthiest city – strong finance and trade career links
Grey, wet, and windy – Hamburg's maritime climate is challenging
German language necessary – fewer English-medium programmes than Berlin

events: Hamburg Harbour Birthday (May) — biggest harbour festival in the world

name: Tongji University
costSource: University data + Numbeo
overview: Tongji University is one of China's most prestigious technical universities, founded in 1907 by German physicians in Shanghai – a heritage that shaped its strong tradition of Sino-German academic exchange. World-renowned for architecture, civil engineering and urban planning, Tongji offers exchange students excellent programs in Shanghai, China's most international and cosmopolitan city.
cityDesc: Shanghai is a large city known for its cosmopolitan atmosphere.

name: Queen's University
costSource: Queen's University Student Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Kingston 2025
overview: Queen's University in Kingston, Ontario is one of Canada's most prestigious universities, with a strong reputation in engineering, commerce, law, medicine, and the arts and sciences — and a loyal, tight-knit alumni community known as one of the most engaged in Canadian higher education. The campus is beautiful, with historic limestone buildings at its heart and a close relationship with the surrounding city that gives it a collegiate small-town character unusual among major research universities. Queen's consistently performs strongly in student satisfaction measures, and the sense of school spirit and community here is palpable. Exchange students find Queen's one of the warmest and most welcoming universities in Canada.
cityDesc: Kingston is a historically rich, walkable city on the shore of Lake Ontario at the point where the lake meets the St Lawrence River and the Rideau Canal — it was Canada's first capital and is filled with 19th-century stone architecture that gives it a distinctive character. It is significantly cheaper than Toronto or Vancouver, and the compact, student-dominated downtown has excellent pubs, restaurants, and live music. Montreal is about 3 hours east and Toronto about 3 hours west, making Kingston a pleasant base between Canada's two largest cities.

perceptions.label: Incredible school spirit and tight-knit student community
Beautiful limestone campus and historic city
Small city with limited job market and nightlife compared to Toronto
Strong alumni network in Canadian business and law
Can feel homogeneous – less diverse than big-city schools

name: University of Gothenburg
costSource: Numbeo Gothenburg 2025; GU housing guide; SEK/USD ~0.092
overview: Founded in 1891, the University of Gothenburg (QS 2025: #201 band) is a major comprehensive research university with strengths in social sciences, health sciences, natural sciences, and the arts. Gothenburg is Sweden's second city and a major port.
cityDesc: Gothenburg is Sweden's most relaxed and social city – a port city with excellent seafood (the best shrimp in Scandinavia), a thriving music scene, and the Archipelago islands accessible by ferry for coastal exploration. Less expensive than Stockholm, and considered friendlier.

Archipelago islands accessible by ferry for outdoor exploration

name: Wuhan University
costSource: WHU housing 2024; Numbeo Wuhan 2025; CNY/USD ~0.138
overview: Founded in 1893, Wuhan University (QS 2025: #275) sits on a hill above East Lake in central Wuhan. Its 1930s architecture campus is routinely cited as China's most beautiful university campus. It has strong programmes in law, Chinese literature, remote sensing, and information management.
cityDesc: Wuhan is China's most centrally located major city – the Yangtze and Han Rivers meet here, historic Yellow Crane Tower, and East Lake (China's largest urban lake). The cherry blossoms on campus (mid-March) draw hundreds of thousands of visitors annually. Wuhan's hot dry noodles (reganmian) are legendary.

name: Emory University
costSource: Emory housing.emory.edu 2024-25; Numbeo Atlanta 2025
overview: Emory University is a leading private research university in Atlanta, Georgia with particular strengths in medicine, public health, law, business, theology, and the social sciences — the Rollins School of Public Health and Emory Healthcare are world-renowned. Its beautiful, tree-lined campus in the Druid Hills neighbourhood of northeast Atlanta has a welcoming, residential feel and is set among some of the city's finest parks and green spaces. Emory consistently ranks among the top 25 universities in the US and benefits from proximity to the CDC, which has offices adjacent to campus. Exchange students find the campus warm, academically stimulating, and richly supported.
cityDesc: Atlanta is one of the South's most vibrant cities — a major business hub, the birthplace of civil rights icons including Martin Luther King Jr., and a city with a thriving food, music, and film industry. The cost of living is moderate by US standards, significantly cheaper than the coasts, and the climate is warm for most of the academic year. Emory's Druid Hills location gives quick access to the city's highlights, including Piedmont Park, the Atlanta BeltLine, and outstanding neighbourhoods like Inman Park and Ponce City Market.

perceptions.label: Atlanta is the American South's most exciting and dynamic major city

cityDesc: Madrid is Spain's vibrant capital – a city of world-class museums (Prado, Reina Sofía, Thyssen), legendary nightlife that starts at midnight, exceptional food from every Spanish region, and a passionate football culture. Cheaper than Barcelona, bigger in spirit.

name: University of Calgary

cityDesc: Calgary is Canada's most outdoor-oriented major city – Banff National Park is 90 minutes west, the Canadian Rockies provide world-class skiing (Lake Louise, Sunshine Village) within 90 minutes, and the Stampede (world's largest rodeo) in July is a defining cultural experience. Calgary itself is clean, prosperous, and less expensive than Toronto or Vancouver.

name: UCLouvain

overview: UCLouvain is one of Belgium's most prestigious universities and the leading French-language Catholic university in Europe. Built in the 1970s as a purpose-designed university city, Louvain-la-Neuve is entirely pedestrianised and built for students – a unique, lively campus community with excellent academic programs across all disciplines.

name: Queen's University Belfast
costSource: QUB Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Belfast 2025
overview: Queen's University Belfast is Northern Ireland's leading research university and a Russell Group member, with particular strengths in medicine, engineering, politics, law, and the arts and humanities. The red-brick campus at the heart of Belfast's vibrant Queen's Quarter has a genuinely beautiful Victorian grandeur, and the close-knit student community reflects the warmth and humour of the city around it. Research at Queen's is globally significant in areas including cancer research, sustainability, and conflict transformation — the latter particularly resonant in a city that has transformed dramatically since the peace process. Exchange students find Belfast one of the most unexpectedly exciting and affordable university cities in the British Isles.
cityDesc: Belfast is a city of remarkable energy and resilience — its Cathedral Quarter has become one of the UK and Ireland's best nightlife and food destinations, the Titanic Quarter is a world-class museum district, and the murals and political history give the city a depth and complexity unlike anywhere else. The cost of living is among the lowest of any capital city in the British Isles, making exchange life very comfortable here. The Causeway Coast and the Mourne Mountains are easily accessible for spectacular weekend escapes.

name: Ohio State University
costSource: OSU University Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Columbus 2025
overview: The Ohio State University is one of America's largest and most comprehensive public universities, with exceptional programmes in business, engineering, education, medicine, agricultural sciences, and the social sciences, all supported by research funding that consistently places it among the top public universities nationally. Its vast campus in Columbus, Ohio is effectively a city within a city — with its own hospitals, arts venues, sports facilities, and research parks. The Buckeyes' football programme is one of the most storied in college sports, and the atmosphere in Ohio Stadium on game day is genuinely electric. Exchange students find the sheer scale of OSU's resources extraordinary, and Columbus itself has become one of the Midwest's most exciting cities.
cityDesc: Columbus is one of America's fastest-growing and most underrated cities — with an outstanding food scene anchored by the Short North Arts District and North Market, a thriving tech and start-up ecosystem, and a young, educated population. The city's flat geography makes cycling practical, and Ohio's position in the Midwest means road trips to Chicago, Pittsburgh, Cincinnati, or the Great Lakes are all accessible.

cityDesc: Tel Aviv is a vibrant, sun-soaked Mediterranean city with stunning beaches, legendary nightlife, extraordinary food, and the highest concentration of tech start-ups outside Silicon Valley. It is one of the world's most LGBTQ-friendly cities.

name: University of Florida
costSource: UF Housing 2024-25; Numbeo Gainesville FL 2025
overview: The University of Florida is a flagship public research university in Gainesville with top programmes in engineering, business, agriculture, health sciences, law, and the liberal arts — and as part of the Association of American Universities, it sits among the nation's most research-intensive institutions.
